parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, decriminalisation (2021) and criminalised orientation-discrimination (up to two years) remove the custody-execution tier entirely, and a visible trans public presence plus 2019 reform-leadership recognition are documented positives. Against that, the 2024 shadow reports find protection on paper unmatched by practice: persistent discrimination, under-investigated violence, and a June 2024 case of a trans woman beaten, arbitrarily detained and subjected to degrading treatment by police — state-perpetrated, recent, remedy still pending. Public acceptance is split (49% poll, 2005 media hostility). Border treatment, prison placement, facilities and minor-specific effects are all not documented, so thin-data extrapolation applies: structural decriminalisation pulls up, implementation failure and police conduct pull down.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry or visa provisions recorded; no documented document-mismatch screening. Gender-marker change unavailable domestically, but the traveller's home passport governs.
entry_documents.protection: Decriminalised status and no recorded entry bar specific to trans travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Unresolved: dossier cannot say how officers read a home passport marker differing from presentation at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: June 2024: trans woman physically attacked by police, arbitrarily detained and subjected to degrading treatment; shadow reports describe under-investigated violence generally.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Judicial military police opened an investigation; arbitrary detention and degrading treatment are legally actionable.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A police encounter after outing converts a service or street dispute into state custody exposure; prison placement rules are undocumented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation documented; no source compares localities, so uniformity cannot be assumed.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single national statutory framework; one officially recognised LGBT organisation operating in three cities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Advocacy capacity concentrated in the capital may thin out for travellers elsewhere.

care_services.exposure: 2024 shadow report documents persistent discrimination across health, education and employment; no LGBTQ-specific facilities recorded.
care_services.protection: Statute criminalises orientation-based discrimination in services; people with HIV are legally entitled to care.
care_services.interaction: Paper entitlement with documented refusal means a traveller denied care may have a claim that does not operate in time.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police attack and degrading treatment framed around gender identity (June 2024); implementation gap acknowledged by local organisations.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Anti-discrimination offence covering orientation; constitutional identity, privacy, liberty and torture protections (gender not enumerated in Art. 23).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: General-rights protection must be invoked case-by-case rather than as an enumerated ground, weakening its practical force.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented: no youth- or minor-specific findings on travel, medication or education.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family would inherit the same undocumented border and service treatment as the adult, with no additional record either way.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Under-investigated violence documented in 2024 shadow report; hostile media framing recorded in 2005; 49% poll support shows divided public acceptance.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Visible mainstream trans public figure (2012); recognised LGBT organisation; investigation into the 2024 police attack.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Conservative social climate plus police conduct means an outing on the street can escalate into a state encounter.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Implementation gap repeatedly documented by shadow reports (2024 regional and UN submissions); constitutional ground for gender absent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Discrimination itself is a criminal offence; constitutional identity/privacy/liberty rights; active civil society documenting violations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist in law but are not shown operating for trans complainants; investigation of the 2024 case is the one live test.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia's routine police stops, phone confiscation and forced interviews with quasi-penal fines describe a continuous pattern. This dossier documents one recent state-perpetrated attack with an open investigation and no routine checkpoint regime, so it sits above 0.35-B, though the police-perpetrator overlap is worse than mere friction.

Valdoria's uneven districts, prolonged verification holds and remedies that cannot compel release resemble this dossier's implementation gap and weak remedy record. This jurisdiction has fewer documented routine checkpoint encounters but a more severe documented police custody incident, placing it roughly at this tier.

Qorinda shows courts delivering injunction, damages, fine and deletion against a discriminatory landlord. Here remedies are statutory but unproven for trans complainants, with violence merely 'under-investigated' — no demonstrated redress, so this rates below 0.65-C.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is decriminalisation plus a criminalised discrimination statute sitting over an implementation gap. For an outed visitor the worst documented pathway is a police encounter producing violence, arbitrary detention and degrading treatment — state-perpetrated, recent, remedy pending. Service discrimination is documented at scale while the entitlement to complain is real but not shown working. Border treatment, custody placement, facilities and minor-specific effects are all not documented; thin-data extrapolation from structural signals (no criminalisation, reform leadership, functioning civil society) pulls upward, from implementation failure and police conduct downward. Net: elevated-to-reduced boundary, no catastrophic tier features.
